text: The following question stood in the name of  Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim –   5 To ask the Minister for Home Affairs (a) what is the (i) average (ii) longest and (iii) shortest time it takes for the Anti-Scam Centre (ASC) to investigate scam cases thus far; and (b) does the ASC provide guidance to individuals who experience frozen accounts to appeal to the courts under section 35(8) of the Criminal Procedure Code.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: In that sense, every case in terms of investigation time differs significantly.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: The freeze on the bank accounts will be lifted upon completion of investigations.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Persons whose bank accounts are frozen can make an application to the Courts to withdraw money for reasonable living or legitimate expenses.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Where asked, the Police will inform account holders of this possibility and advise them to seek legal advice.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
text: Nowadays, bank accounts are absolutely essential for daily living because if the bank account is frozen, it could severely impact the person's ability to conduct daily transactions like receiving their salary.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
text: My first supplementary question is, the Minister of State mentioned that they can apply to conduct some limited transactions, does this include being able to receive their salary into their bank accounts?

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Indeed, we recognise that victims of scams require their bank accounts to be able to make daily transactions.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: We all recognise the importance of having a bank account to facilitate these transactions.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: I think the difficulty that the Police faces is that during investigations, some of these bank accounts, unfortunately, from the victim's perspective, they are absolutely a victim in the absolute sense.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: But what has happened to some of these accounts is that they may be also tainted with the sense that scam monies may also have been remitted into these accounts, because when a scam syndicate operates, we often see that monies are transferred from one bank account to another and there is often co-mingling of monies in bank accounts.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: So, the Police actually has to freeze the relevant bank accounts for the purposes of investigations.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: The Police freezes these bank accounts when there are two instances.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: So, the victim from your perspective, victim A for instance, may see himself or herself as the victim who has transferred monies out.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: But actually, if you look at the entire scam syndicates and its operations, this particular victim A's bank account, could have been compromised whereby another victim's monies has been transferred in as well.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Number two, as part of fund tracing investigations, because for instance, in a job scam, it can impact hundreds of persons at the same time.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: So, as part of tracing the flows of monies, they will have to freeze many bank accounts and you will often see that there are multiple claimants on the specific sums of monies.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: I just wanted to share that this is the background as to why the Police has to freeze bank accounts.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: And we do not want to unnecessarily impede the victims' ability to transact on a bank account, so we would typically recommend that they set up a separate bank account, to be able to receive their salaries.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: On your second point, there are various reasons why a bank account can be blacklisted.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: A victim, like I mentioned before, they themselves see themselves as a victim in the absolute sense, but unfortunately their bank account has been compromised, it could have been used almost in a sense like a money mule, because monies have been transferred in and out of the account.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: So, there could be various reasons why an account is blacklisted.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: So, I think it differs on a case-by-case basis.
